_note: DRAFT for review. General guidance only; no chemical doses. Always follow local agricultural extension advice and product labels.

unknown_plant.title: Not a supported plant / unclear photo
unknown_plant.summary: This does not look like one of the supported crops, or the photo is unclear.
actions: Photograph a single leaf, filling the frame, in daylight.
Avoid fruit, stems, whole fields or text/diagrams.

apple__scab.title: Apple scab
apple__scab.cause: Fungus (Venturia inaequalis), spreads in cool wet spring weather.
signs: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves
Leaves may yellow, curl and drop early
Dark corky spots on fruit
actions: Remove and destroy fallen and infected leaves.
Prune to open the canopy so leaves dry faster.
If severe, ask local extension which fungicide is approved for apples in your area.

apple__black_rot.title: Apple black rot / frogeye leaf spot
apple__black_rot.cause: Fungus (Botryosphaeria obtusa), survives on dead wood and mummified fruit.
signs: Round brown spots with purple edges (frogeye) on leaves
Rotting fruit that turns brown to black
Cankers on branches
actions: Prune out dead or cankered branches and remove mummified fruit.
Destroy infected material away from the orchard.
Ask local extension about approved fungicides if pressure is high.
prevention: Clean up fruit and debris each season

apple__rust.title: Cedar apple rust
apple__rust.cause: Fungus (Gymnosporangium) that needs both apple and juniper/cedar trees.
signs: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface
Small tube-like structures under the spots later in the season
actions: Remove nearby juniper/cedar galls if practical.
Ask local extension about preventive fungicide timing in spring.

apple__healthy.title: Healthy apple leaf
actions: Water at the base, not on leaves.
Feed in spring according to a soil test.

bell_pepper__bacterial_spot.title: Bacterial spot (pepper)
bell_pepper__bacterial_spot.cause: Bacteria (Xanthomonas), spread by splashing water and infected seed.
signs: Small dark water-soaked spots that turn brown with yellow halo
Spots may merge; leaves yellow and drop
Raised scabby spots on fruit
actions: Remove badly infected plants and leaves.
Avoid working with wet plants and avoid overhead watering.
Copper-based products are sometimes used; check local advice and the label.

blueberry__healthy.title: Healthy blueberry leaf
actions: Prune old canes to improve airflow.

cherry__powdery_mildew.title: Powdery mildew (cherry)
cherry__powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus (Podosphaera), favoured by warm days, cool humid nights.
signs: White powdery coating on leaves
Leaves may curl or distort
actions: Ask local extension about approved fungicides if severe.
prevention: Plant in sun with good airflow

corn__common_rust.title: Common rust (corn)
corn__common_rust.cause: Fungus (Puccinia sorghi), spread by wind in cool humid weather.
signs: Small round to oval brick-red or brown raised pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules turn dark with age
actions: Often mild; monitor spread to upper leaves.
If severe before tasselling, ask local extension about fungicide.

corn__gray_leaf_spot.title: Gray leaf spot (corn)
corn__gray_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Cercospora zeae-maydis), survives in crop residue; warm humid weather.
signs: Narrow rectangular tan to gray spots running parallel to leaf veins
Spots may merge and kill large leaf areas
actions: Rotate away from corn and till or manage residue.
Ask local extension about fungicide if the upper leaves are affected.

corn__northern_leaf_blight.title: Northern leaf blight (corn)
corn__northern_leaf_blight.cause: Fungus (Exserohilum turcicum), cool moist weather, survives in residue.
signs: Long cigar-shaped gray-green to tan lesions, often 2.5-15 cm
Lesions can join and blight the whole leaf
actions: Ask local extension about fungicide if it reaches upper leaves early.

corn__healthy.title: Healthy corn leaf
actions: Keep up regular nitrogen and water, especially at tasselling.
Scout weekly for spots or pustules.

grape__black_rot.title: Black rot (grape)
grape__black_rot.cause: Fungus (Guignardia bidwellii), warm wet weather; overwinters on mummified berries.
signs: Tan circular leaf spots with dark borders and tiny black dots
Berries shrivel into hard black mummies
actions: Remove mummified berries and infected canes.
Ask local extension about fungicide timing from early growth stages.

grape__leaf_blight.title: Grape leaf blight / leaf spot
grape__leaf_blight.cause: Fungal leaf spot (e.g. Isariopsis), favoured by humid conditions.
signs: Irregular dark brown spots on leaves
Leaves may yellow and drop early
actions: Improve airflow through pruning and trellising.
Ask local extension about fungicide if it spreads.

grape__healthy.title: Healthy grape leaf
actions: Keep the canopy open and trained.

peach__healthy.title: Healthy peach leaf
actions: Prune for airflow in dormant season.

potato__early_blight.title: Early blight (potato)
potato__early_blight.cause: Fungus (Alternaria solani), stressed plants, warm humid conditions.
signs: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target look) on older leaves first
Yellowing around spots
actions: Keep plants well fed and watered (stress makes it worse).
Ask local extension about fungicide if it spreads.

potato__late_blight.title: Late blight (potato)
potato__late_blight.cause: Oomycete (Phytophthora infestans); spreads very fast in cool wet weather. Serious disease.
signs: Large water-soaked dark patches, often with pale green edge
White fuzzy growth under leaves in humid weather
Tubers rot
actions: Act quickly: remove and bag infected plants; do not compost.
Do not harvest tubers from badly infected plants for storage.
Contact local extension urgently for approved fungicides.

potato__healthy.title: Healthy potato leaf
actions: Scout weekly, especially in cool wet weather.

soybean__healthy.title: Healthy soybean leaf
actions: Scout weekly for spots or yellowing.

squash__powdery_mildew.title: Powdery mildew (squash)
squash__powdery_mildew.cause: Fungi, thrive in warm dry days and humid nights.
signs: White powdery patches on leaf surfaces
Leaves yellow, then brown and die
actions: Ask local extension about approved treatments.
prevention: Water at the base in morning

strawberry__leaf_scorch.title: Leaf scorch (strawberry)
signs: Many small purple spots that enlarge
Leaf edges look scorched and dry
actions: Ask local extension about fungicide if severe.

tomato__bacterial_spot.title: Bacterial spot (tomato)
tomato__bacterial_spot.cause: Bacteria (Xanthomonas), spread by splashing water; warm wet weather.
signs: Small dark greasy-looking spots on leaves, sometimes with yellow halo
Rough scabby spots on fruit
actions: Remove badly infected leaves; avoid handling wet plants.
Copper products are sometimes used; check local advice.

tomato__early_blight.title: Early blight (tomato)
tomato__early_blight.cause: Fungus (Alternaria solani), warm humid weather; affects stressed plants.
signs: Brown spots with concentric rings, starting on older lower leaves
Yellowing around spots
actions: Mulch and water at the base.
Ask local extension about fungicide if it spreads.
prevention: Keep plants well fed and watered

tomato__late_blight.title: Late blight (tomato)
tomato__late_blight.cause: Oomycete (Phytophthora infestans); spreads very fast in cool wet weather. Serious disease.
signs: Large greasy dark patches on leaves, often with pale edge
White fuzz underneath in humid weather
Firm brown rot on fruit
actions: Act quickly: remove and bag infected plants; do not compost.
Contact local extension urgently for approved fungicides.

tomato__leaf_mold.title: Leaf mold (tomato)
tomato__leaf_mold.cause: Fungus (Passalora fulva), high humidity, common in greenhouses.
signs: Pale green-yellow patches on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mold underneath
actions: Ask local extension about fungicides if severe.

tomato__septoria_leaf_spot.title: Septoria leaf spot (tomato)
tomato__septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Septoria lycopersici), splashing water, warm wet weather.
signs: Many small round spots with dark borders and gray centres, often with tiny black dots
Starts on lower leaves
actions: Ask local extension about fungicide if it climbs the plant.

tomato__mosaic_virus.title: Mosaic virus (tomato)
tomato__mosaic_virus.cause: Virus (ToMV/TMV), spread by hands, tools, seed. No cure.
signs: Mottled light and dark green mosaic pattern
Leaves may be curled, narrow or distorted
Stunted growth
actions: Remove and bag infected plants; do not compost.
Wash hands and tools with soap or disinfectant between plants.
Do not smoke or handle tobacco before touching plants.

tomato__yellow_leaf_curl_virus.title: Yellow leaf curl virus (tomato)
tomato__yellow_leaf_curl_virus.cause: Virus spread by whiteflies. No cure.
signs: Upward-curling, yellow-edged, small leaves
Stunted bushy plants
Few or no fruit
actions: Remove and bag infected plants early.
Control whiteflies (yellow sticky traps, netting; ask local advice).
Do not move plants from infected areas.

tomato__healthy.title: Healthy tomato leaf
actions: Stake and prune lower leaves for airflow.
Scout weekly, especially in humid weather.

banana__healthy.title: Healthy banana leaf
actions: Keep soil well drained and mulched.
Scout for yellowing of older leaves.

banana__panama_disease.title: Panama disease (Fusarium wilt, banana)
banana__panama_disease.cause: Soil-borne fungus (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense) entering through roots. No cure.
signs: Older leaves yellow, then collapse around the stem
Brown to reddish discolouration inside the stem when cut
Plants wilt and die
actions: Remove and destroy infected plants; do not move soil or suckers from the area.
Clean tools and boots between plots.
Contact local agricultural extension: this disease is often notifiable.
prevention: Improve drainage and avoid moving soil

basil__healthy.title: Healthy basil leaf
actions: Water at the base in the morning.
Pinch flowers and tips for bushy growth.

basil__downy_mildew.title: Downy mildew (basil)
basil__downy_mildew.cause: Oomycete (Peronospora belbahrii), spreads in humid conditions and on infected seed.
signs: Yellowing between leaf veins
Grey to purple fuzzy growth under leaves
Leaves curl and brown
actions: Remove and bag infected leaves or plants.
Improve airflow and keep leaves dry.
Ask local extension about options; fungicides are limited.

bean__healthy.title: Healthy bean leaf
actions: Scout for spots and mosaic patterns.

bean__halo_blight.title: Halo blight (bean)
bean__halo_blight.cause: Bacteria (Pseudomonas syringae pv. phaseolicola), seed-borne, spread by rain splash in cool weather.
signs: Small water-soaked spots with a yellow-green halo
Spots turn brown; leaves may drop
Pods get greasy spots
actions: Avoid working in the crop when wet.
Ask local extension about copper-based options.

bean__mosaic_virus.title: Bean mosaic virus
bean__mosaic_virus.cause: Virus spread by aphids and infected seed. No cure.
signs: Light and dark green mottling
Puckered, curled leaves
Stunted plants and poor pods
actions: Do not save seed from infected plants.

bean__rust.title: Rust (bean)
bean__rust.cause: Fungus (Uromyces appendiculatus), spreads by wind in humid, mild weather.
signs: Small rusty-brown powdery pustules on leaves
Yellow patches around them
Early leaf drop
actions: Remove infected leaves and plant debris.
Keep leaves dry and improve spacing.
Ask local extension about fungicide if severe.

blueberry__rust.title: Rust (blueberry)
blueberry__rust.cause: Fungus that alternates with another host plant (often hemlock or conifers).
signs: Small yellow to orange pustules under leaves
Yellow spots on top
Early leaf drop
actions: Ask local extension about fungicide timing.

broccoli__downy_mildew.title: Downy mildew (broccoli)
signs: Yellow to brown angular patches on upper leaves
White-grey fuzz underneath
Dark spots on heads
actions: Improve airflow and avoid wetting leaves.
Ask local extension about treatments if severe.

cabbage__healthy.title: Healthy cabbage leaf
actions: Check under leaves for caterpillars and aphids.

cabbage__alternaria_leaf_spot.title: Alternaria leaf spot (cabbage)
cabbage__alternaria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Alternaria brassicicola), spread by seed, splash and wind in warm humid weather.
signs: Round brown spots with concentric rings
Yellow halo around spots
Spots may crack and join
actions: Ask local extension about fungicides if severe.

carrot__cavity_spot.title: Cavity spot (carrot)
carrot__cavity_spot.cause: Soil-borne Pythium fungi in wet, compacted soil. Mostly affects the root.
signs: Sunken elliptical lesions on the root
Leaves may yellow in severe cases

cauliflower__alternaria_leaf_spot.title: Alternaria leaf spot (cauliflower)
signs: Brown spots with rings on leaves
Yellow edges around spots
Dark spots on curds
actions: Ask local extension about fungicides if it spreads.

celery__anthracnose.title: Anthracnose (celery)
celery__anthracnose.cause: Fungal disease (Colletotrichum or Septoria-like), splashing water and humid weather.
signs: Small dark sunken spots on leaves and stalks
Spots join and leaves collapse

celery__early_blight.title: Early blight (celery, Cercospora)
signs: Small yellow-green spots that turn tan with a darker edge
Older leaves affected first

citrus__canker.title: Citrus canker
citrus__canker.cause: Bacteria (Xanthomonas citri), spread by rain and wind; can be a regulated disease.
signs: Raised corky lesions with a yellow halo on leaves
Spots on fruit and twigs
Leaf and fruit drop
actions: Report to local agricultural authority: it is often notifiable.
Remove and bag infected material; disinfect tools.

citrus__greening.title: Citrus greening (HLB)
citrus__greening.cause: Bacterium spread by psyllid insects. No cure. Often notifiable.
signs: Blotchy yellow mottling on leaves
Small lopsided bitter fruit
Twig dieback
actions: Remove infected trees as advised locally.

coffee__leaf_rust.title: Coffee leaf rust
coffee__leaf_rust.cause: Fungus (Hemileia vastatrix), spreads by wind and rain in warm humid weather.
signs: Yellow-orange powdery spots under leaves
Matching pale spots on top
Leaf drop and weak plants
actions: Remove heavily infected leaves where practical.
Ask local extension about fungicide timing.

cucumber__angular_leaf_spot.title: Angular leaf spot (cucumber)
cucumber__angular_leaf_spot.cause: Bacteria (Pseudomonas syringae pv. lachrymans), spread by splash and seed.
signs: Water-soaked angular spots limited by veins
Spots dry, tear and fall out
Spots on fruit
actions: Remove infected leaves; avoid handling wet plants.
Ask local extension about copper options.

cucumber__bacterial_wilt.title: Bacterial wilt (cucumber)
cucumber__bacterial_wilt.cause: Bacteria (Erwinia tracheiphila) spread by cucumber beetles. No cure.
signs: Sudden wilting of leaves and vines
Sticky white ooze from cut stems

cucumber__powdery_mildew.title: Powdery mildew (cucumber)
cucumber__powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus, favoured by warm days and humid nights.
signs: White powdery patches on leaves
Leaves yellow, brown and die
actions: Ask local extension about approved treatments.

eggplant__cercospora_leaf_spot.title: Cercospora leaf spot (eggplant)
signs: Round spots with pale centres and dark margins
Leaves yellow and drop

garlic__leaf_blight.title: Leaf blight (garlic)
garlic__leaf_blight.cause: Fungal leaf blights (e.g. Stemphylium, Botrytis), humid weather.
signs: Pale yellow to brown spots or streaks on leaf tips
Leaves dry from the tip down

garlic__rust.title: Rust (garlic)
signs: Small orange powdery pustules on leaves
Leaves yellow and dry early
actions: Ask local extension about fungicides if severe.

ginger__healthy.title: Healthy ginger leaf
actions: Provide partial shade and well-drained soil.

ginger__leaf_spot.title: Leaf spot (ginger)
ginger__leaf_spot.cause: Fungal leaf spot (e.g. Phyllosticta), wet weather.
signs: Oval white to brown spots with a yellow halo
Spots merge and leaves dry

ginger__sheath_blight.title: Sheath blight (ginger)
signs: Water-soaked lesions on leaf sheaths
Lesions spread up and rot stems

lettuce__healthy.title: Healthy lettuce leaf
actions: Water in the morning at the base.

lettuce__downy_mildew.title: Downy mildew (lettuce)
signs: Yellow angular patches on upper leaves
White fuzz underneath
Leaves turn brown

lettuce__mosaic_virus.title: Lettuce mosaic virus
lettuce__mosaic_virus.cause: Virus carried in seed and spread by aphids. No cure.
signs: Mottled, crinkled leaves
Stunted plants
Poor heads
actions: Do not save seed from infected plants.

maple__healthy.title: Healthy maple leaf
actions: Water young trees in dry spells.

maple__tar_spot.title: Tar spot (maple)
maple__tar_spot.cause: Fungus (Rhytisma), spreads by spores in wet spring weather.
signs: Raised black tar-like spots on leaves
Yellow halo around spots
actions: Usually cosmetic; healthy trees tolerate it.

plum__healthy.title: Healthy plum leaf
actions: Prune in dry weather for airflow.

plum__pocket_disease.title: Plum pocket (pocket plum)
plum__pocket_disease.cause: Fungus (Taphrina communis) infecting flowers and young fruit in cool wet spring.
signs: Fruit become hollow, swollen and bladder-like
Leaves may be puckered
actions: Remove and destroy affected fruit before they mature.
Ask local extension about spring protectant sprays.

rice__blast.title: Rice blast
rice__blast.cause: Fungus (Magnaporthe oryzae), spreads in humid weather and with heavy nitrogen use.
signs: Diamond-shaped grey spots with brown margins on leaves
Neck rot at the panicle in severe cases
actions: Ask local extension about fungicide timing.

rice__sheath_blight.title: Sheath blight (rice)
rice__sheath_blight.cause: Fungus (Rhizoctonia solani), dense crops and high humidity.
signs: Oval greenish-grey lesions on the sheath near the water line
Lesions spread upward
actions: Reduce plant density and excess nitrogen.

tobacco__mosaic_virus.title: Tobacco mosaic virus
tobacco__mosaic_virus.cause: Virus spread by contact (hands, tools). No cure.
signs: Mottled light and dark green leaves
Distorted, narrow leaves
Stunted growth
actions: Do not smoke or handle tobacco before touching plants.

zucchini__yellow_mosaic_virus.title: Zucchini yellow mosaic virus
zucchini__yellow_mosaic_virus.cause: Virus spread by aphids. No cure.
signs: Yellow mosaic patches on leaves
Distorted, narrow leaves
Bumpy deformed fruit

apple__mosaic_virus.title: Apple mosaic virus
apple__mosaic_virus.cause: Virus spread by grafting and infected stock. No cure.
signs: Cream to yellow patches or bands on leaves
Reduced vigour
actions: Report severe cases to local advisers.
Do not graft from infected trees.

cherry__leaf_spot.title: Cherry leaf spot
signs: Small purple spots turning brown, with holes ('shot-hole')
Yellow leaves that drop early
actions: Ask local extension about spray timing.

corn__smut.title: Corn smut
signs: Large grey-white swollen galls on ears, stalks or leaves
Galls turn black and burst into spores
actions: Remove and destroy galls before they burst.

grape__downy_mildew.title: Downy mildew (grape)
signs: Yellow oily patches on upper leaf surface
White downy growth underneath
Shrivelled berries
actions: Ask local extension about spray programme.

grape__esca.title: Esca / black measles (grape)
signs: Yellow or red 'tiger stripe' pattern between veins
Dark spots on berries
Vine decline
actions: Mark and prune out affected wood in dry weather.

grape__leafroll_disease.title: Grapevine leafroll disease
grape__leafroll_disease.cause: Virus spread by mealybugs and infected planting material. No cure.
signs: Leaf edges roll downward
Red or yellow colour between green veins in autumn
Reduced yield

peach__bacterial_spot.title: Bacterial spot (peach)
peach__bacterial_spot.cause: Bacteria (Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni), spread by rain.
signs: Small dark angular spots on leaves
Spots drop out leaving holes
Pitted fruit
actions: Ask local extension about copper options.

peach__leaf_curl.title: Peach leaf curl
peach__leaf_curl.cause: Fungus (Taphrina deformans), infects buds in cool wet spring.
signs: Thickened, red-pink puckered curled leaves
Leaves later turn grey and drop
actions: Apply protection only in late winter before bud swell: ask local extension.

strawberry__anthracnose.title: Anthracnose (strawberry)
signs: Dark sunken lesions on runners and stalks
Leaf spots
Plant wilting and crown rot

tomato__spider_mites.title: Spider mites (tomato)
tomato__spider_mites.cause: Tiny mites (Tetranychus urticae) feeding on leaves; worse in hot dry weather.
signs: Fine yellow stippling on leaves
Fine webbing under leaves
Leaves bronze and dry
actions: Spray leaves with water to knock mites off.
Ask local extension about miticides or beneficial predators.

tomato__target_spot.title: Target spot (tomato)
signs: Brown spots with concentric rings on leaves
Spots on fruit

banana__anthracnose.title: Anthracnose (banana)
banana__anthracnose.cause: Fungus (Colletotrichum musae), spreads by rain splash in warm humid weather.
signs: Dark brown to black sunken spots on leaves or fruit
Spots may have a yellow edge
Affected areas dry and crack
actions: Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruit.
Handle fruit gently to avoid wounds.
Ask local extension about approved fungicides if severe.
prevention: Keep the plantation clean of dead leaves

banana__bunchy_top.title: Bunchy top virus (banana)
banana__bunchy_top.cause: Virus spread by banana aphids and by infected planting material. No cure.
signs: Dark green streaks on leaf veins and stalks
New leaves are short, narrow and bunched at the top
Plant is stunted and gives little or no fruit
actions: Remove and destroy infected plants including the roots.
Report to the local agriculture office: it is often notifiable.
prevention: Do not move suckers from infected areas

banana__cordana_leaf_spot.title: Cordana leaf spot (banana)
banana__cordana_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Cordana musae), favoured by wet weather and humid plantations.
signs: Large oval spots with a pale centre and a yellow edge
Spots often start at the leaf margin
Spots may merge and dry out large areas
actions: Improve air flow by thinning and weeding.
Ask local extension if it keeps spreading.

banana__sigatoka.title: Sigatoka leaf spot (banana)
banana__sigatoka.cause: Fungus (Mycosphaerella species, black and yellow Sigatoka), spreads by wind and rain in warm humid weather.
signs: Small yellow or brown streaks on the leaf that grow into dark spots with a yellow halo
Spots join and large parts of the leaf turn brown and die
Leaves collapse early and the plant weakens
actions: Cut off and destroy badly affected leaves.
Improve drainage and plant spacing for air flow.
Ask local extension which fungicide programme is approved in your area.

banana__bract_mosaic_virus.title: Bract mosaic virus (banana)
banana__bract_mosaic_virus.cause: Virus spread by aphids and infected planting material. No cure.
signs: Reddish-brown streaks on leaves, stems and the flower bract
Streaks run across the leaf vein
Poor, small bunches
actions: Do not use suckers from infected plants.

banana__moko_disease.title: Moko disease (banana)
banana__moko_disease.cause: Soil and insect-spread bacterium (Ralstonia solanacearum). No cure. Often notifiable.
signs: Young leaves turn yellow and then collapse
Brown to black discolouration inside the stem when cut
Fruit ripens unevenly and rots inside
actions: Report to the local agriculture authority.
Remove and destroy infected plants; do not move soil or plant parts.
Disinfect tools and boots between plots.
prevention: Control insects that visit the flowers

banana__pestalotiopsis_leaf_spot.title: Pestalotiopsis leaf spot (banana)
banana__pestalotiopsis_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Pestalotiopsis), often enters through wounds in wet weather.
signs: Dark brown spots with grey centres and a yellow edge
Spots join into larger dead patches
Leaf edges dry and tear
actions: Ask local extension if the spots keep spreading.

blueberry__scorch.title: Blueberry scorch virus
blueberry__scorch.cause: Virus spread by aphids and infected plants. No cure.
signs: Flowers and young leaves turn brown suddenly as if scorched
Blossoms wilt and drop
Shoots die back from the tip
actions: Contact local extension: this virus is often regulated.
prevention: Do not move plants from infected fields

broccoli__alternaria_leaf_spot.title: Alternaria leaf spot (broccoli)
broccoli__alternaria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Alternaria), spreads by seed, wind and splashing water in warm humid weather.
signs: Round brown spots with rings like a target
Yellow halo around the spots
Spots can reach the head
actions: Keep leaves dry; water at the base.
Ask local extension about approved fungicides if it spreads.

cabbage__black_rot.title: Black rot (cabbage)
cabbage__black_rot.cause: Bacterium (Xanthomonas campestris), seed-borne, spreads by rain splash and in warm humid weather.
signs: Yellow V-shaped patches starting at the leaf edge
Veins turn black inside the patch
Leaves wither and the head may rot
actions: Avoid working in the crop when wet.
Ask local extension about options; there is no cure once it starts.
prevention: Rotate with non-cabbage crops for 2-3 years
Control weeds in the cabbage family

cabbage__downy_mildew.title: Downy mildew (cabbage)
signs: Yellow to brown angular patches on upper leaf surface
White-grey fuzz underneath in humid weather
Dark spots on the head
actions: Improve air flow and avoid wetting leaves.
Ask local extension about treatments if severe.
prevention: Water in the morning at the base

carrot__alternaria_leaf_blight.title: Alternaria leaf blight (carrot)
carrot__alternaria_leaf_blight.cause: Fungus (Alternaria dauci), spreads in warm humid weather and on seed.
signs: Dark brown to black spots with a yellow halo on leaf edges
Leaves curl, yellow and die
Tops collapse and roots can be small
actions: Ask local extension about approved fungicides if severe.

coffee__brown_eye_spot.title: Brown eye spot (coffee)
coffee__brown_eye_spot.cause: Fungus (Cercospora coffeicola), worse in plants stressed by sun, drought or poor feeding.
signs: Round brown spots with a pale centre and a yellow ring
Spots on leaves and berries
Leaves drop early
actions: Improve feeding and shade; stressed plants get it more.
Remove heavily spotted leaves where practical.

coffee__leaf_miner.title: Leaf miner damage (coffee)
coffee__leaf_miner.cause: Tiny insect larvae (Leucoptera coffeella) that tunnel inside the leaf. It is a pest, not a fungus.
signs: Irregular pale or brown blotches on the upper leaf
Blotches look like blisters and later tear
Leaves drop early
actions: Ask local extension about leaf miner control.
Protect natural enemies such as wasps.
prevention: Regular checks in the dry season

coffee__phoma_leaf_spot.title: Phoma leaf spot (coffee)
coffee__phoma_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Phoma), favoured by cool wet weather and strong wind.
signs: Dark brown to black spots on young leaves and shoot tips
Spots may merge and kill the tip
Leaves curl and drop
actions: Remove and destroy affected tips and leaves.
Ask local extension about approved options.

soybean__bacterial_blight.title: Bacterial blight (soybean)
soybean__bacterial_blight.cause: Bacterium (Pseudomonas savastanoi pv. glycinea), spreads by rain splash and wind in cool wet weather.
signs: Small angular water-soaked spots that turn brown
Yellow halo around the spots
Spots join and the middle may fall out

soybean__brown_spot.title: Brown spot (soybean)
soybean__brown_spot.cause: Fungus (Septoria glycines), survives on residue; warm wet weather.
signs: Small dark brown irregular spots on lower leaves first
Leaves yellow and drop early
Spots may join
actions: Ask local extension about fungicide if it climbs the plant.

soybean__downy_mildew.title: Downy mildew (soybean)
soybean__downy_mildew.cause: Oomycete (Peronospora manshurica), cool humid weather; survives on seed and residue.
signs: Pale green to yellow patches on upper leaf surface
Grey fuzz underneath in humid weather
Patches turn brown and dry
actions: Ask local extension about options if severe.

soybean__frogeye_leaf_spot.title: Frogeye leaf spot (soybean)
soybean__frogeye_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Cercospora sojina), warm humid weather; survives on seed and residue.
signs: Round to angular spots with a grey centre and a reddish-brown border
Spots on the upper leaf surface
Spots may join and kill leaf parts
actions: Ask local extension about fungicide if it spreads.

soybean__rust.title: Rust (soybean)
soybean__rust.cause: Fungus (Phakopsora pachyrhizi), spreads quickly by wind in warm humid weather. Serious disease.
signs: Tiny tan to reddish-brown spots, mostly on the underside
Small raised pustules in the spots
Leaves yellow and drop early
actions: Contact local extension urgently about fungicide timing.
Remove volunteer soybean and alternate host plants.

tobacco__blue_mold.title: Blue mold (tobacco)
tobacco__blue_mold.cause: Oomycete (Peronospora tabacina), spreads by wind in cool damp weather. Spreads very fast.
signs: Yellow patches on upper leaf surface
Grey-blue fuzz underneath
Leaves curl and die
actions: Act quickly; remove infected seedlings or plants.
Improve air flow and reduce leaf wetness.

tobacco__brown_spot.title: Brown spot (tobacco)
tobacco__brown_spot.cause: Fungus (Alternaria alternata), favoured by warm humid weather and older plants.
signs: Round brown spots with rings, starting on lower leaves
Spots may have a yellow edge
Leaves tear and dry out
actions: Ask local extension about options if severe.

wheat__healthy.title: Healthy wheat leaf
actions: Scout weekly for rust pustules or spots.

wheat__bacterial_leaf_streak.title: Bacterial leaf streak / black chaff (wheat)
wheat__bacterial_leaf_streak.cause: Bacterium (Xanthomonas translucens), seed-borne, spreads by rain and wind.
signs: Narrow water-soaked streaks along the leaf
Streaks turn brown or yellow with a shiny surface
Dark streaks on the ear (black chaff)
actions: Ask local extension about options; there is no cure.

wheat__leaf_rust.title: Leaf rust (wheat)
wheat__leaf_rust.cause: Fungus (Puccinia triticina), spreads by wind in mild humid weather.
signs: Small round orange-brown pustules scattered on the leaf
Pustules mostly on the upper side
Leaves yellow and die early
actions: Check nearby fields and scout weekly.
Ask local extension about fungicide timing.

wheat__powdery_mildew.title: Powdery mildew (wheat)
wheat__powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus (Blumeria graminis), favoured by cool humid weather and dense crops.
signs: White powdery patches on leaves and stems
Patches turn grey-brown with small black dots
Leaves yellow and dry
actions: Avoid very dense sowing and excess nitrogen.
Ask local extension about fungicide if severe.

wheat__septoria_blotch.title: Septoria leaf blotch (wheat)
wheat__septoria_blotch.cause: Fungus (Zymoseptoria tritici), spreads by rain splash in cool wet weather; survives on residue.
signs: Pale yellow to brown blotches, often rectangular
Tiny black dots inside the blotches
Lower leaves first, then upwards
actions: Ask local extension about fungicide timing.

wheat__stem_rust.title: Stem rust (wheat)
wheat__stem_rust.cause: Fungus (Puccinia graminis), spreads fast by wind in warm humid weather. Serious disease.
signs: Dark red-brown raised pustules on stems and leaves
Pustules rough and powdery, often on both sides
Stems weaken and plants lodge
actions: Contact local extension urgently about fungicide.
Remove volunteer wheat and barberry nearby.

wheat__stripe_rust.title: Stripe rust (wheat)
wheat__stripe_rust.cause: Fungus (Puccinia striiformis), spreads by wind in cool moist weather. Serious disease.
signs: Yellow to orange powdery stripes running along the leaf veins
Stripes on leaves and sometimes on the ear
Leaves turn yellow and dry
actions: Ask local extension urgently about fungicide timing.
prevention: Early monitoring in cool wet weather

zucchini__bacterial_wilt.title: Bacterial wilt (zucchini)
zucchini__bacterial_wilt.cause: Bacterium (Erwinia tracheiphila) spread by cucumber beetles. No cure.
signs: Leaves and vines suddenly wilt
Sticky white ooze from cut stems
Plant collapses in days

zucchini__downy_mildew.title: Downy mildew (zucchini)
signs: Yellow angular patches on the upper leaf surface
Grey-purple fuzz underneath in humid weather
Patches turn brown and leaves die
actions: Improve air flow and avoid wetting leaves.
Ask local extension about options if severe.

zucchini__powdery_mildew.title: Powdery mildew (zucchini)
zucchini__powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus (Podosphaera xanthii), warm days and humid nights.
signs: White powdery patches on leaves and stems
Leaves yellow, then brown and die
Plants weaken and fruit is smaller
actions: Ask local extension about approved treatments.
prevention: Water at the base in the morning

diseased_unnamed.title: Looks diseased, disease not identified
diseased_unnamed.summary: The leaf shows signs of disease, but it does not match any disease this app can name.
actions: Do not treat on this result alone.
Show the leaf, or a clear photo, to a local agriculture officer.
Take another photo in daylight, one leaf filling the frame, to check again.

soybean__mosaic_virus.title: Mosaic virus (soybean)
soybean__mosaic_virus.cause: Virus spread by aphids and infected seed. No cure.
signs: Light and dark green mottling
Puckered, curled leaves
Stunted plants and poor pods
actions: Do not save seed from infected plants.
